Hi Sara — thanks for the quick review and the template.

Short answer: yes, we can provide a COI and the endorsement language; there are a couple of practical details to confirm so we match StormByte's procurement expectations:

1) Additional Insured scope: Our standard practice is to grant Additional Insured on the CGL for claims arising out of Redwood's acts or omissions. Can you confirm you need full primary & noncontributory wording vs. a more limited endorsement? If procurement requires the primary & noncontributory clause, we'll need to route to underwriting for carrier sign-off which typically adds 3–7 business days.

2) Retroactive/retro date: This only applies to E&O claims-made policies. Do you require a retroactive date in the endorsement or is affirmation of current policy sufficient?

3) Certificate holder name and address: Please confirm exact entity name (e.g., StormByte, Inc.) and address you want on the COI.

I've attached a draft endorsement wording we typically propose (see endorsement_Wording_draft.docx). I've looped in Olga (insurance operations) and Marcus (legal lead) to confirm if we can expedite the endorsement approval.

Proposed next steps:
- StormByte confirms additional insured scope and certificate holder address (Sara)
- Aegis broker confirms carrier acceptance or flags questions (copied)
- Redwood insurance ops routes endorsement to carrier if primary/noncontrib is required

We can often deliver a COI showing limits within 24–48 hours; the endorsement (if carrier sign-off needed) is the gating item.

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen

> I've attached a draft endorsement wording we typically propose (see endorsement_Wording_draft.docx).

Hi all — quick note from insurance ops.

We pulled the current carrier matrix. If StormByte requires primary & noncontributory additional insured wording on the CGL, one of our carriers (GreatLedge) will accept with an endorsement but they require underwriter approval and an underwriting fee in some cases. If StormByte can accept "primary for liability arising out of Redwood's performance" (noncontributory but limited in scope) we can usually get signed endorsement within 3 business days.

If StormByte absolutely needs broad primary/noncontrib with waiver of subrogation, that's likely a 7–10 business day path and may require either a carrier change or a premium adjustment.

Sara — can you confirm whether StormByte will accept the draft endorsement text we shared, or do they need the broader language? If you prefer, we can have Aegis email the carrier directly — cc'd broker to facilitate.

Thanks — Olga
